cells.tense: You're here, and the ending is in your hands.
cells.verb: giving something that's over a shape it can actually close in
cells.place: the room where what was is being cleared out
cells.ask: Let one thing you don't understand yet stay in the room without filing it — and notice how much still makes sense around you.
cells.core:
You're here, and the ending is in your hands. Something is finishing, and you're the one deciding what goes first, what gets kept, and what the close looks like — not to control it, but so it can actually end instead of trailing off. People can feel that order near you; it makes a hard thing possible to walk through.

That clarity is already doing its job. What it's free to do next is trust the part that doesn't come from arranging: the knowing that lands before you've sorted it. Let one thing you don't understand yet stay in the room without filing it — and notice how much still makes sense around you.
cells.sheetLine: You're giving the ending a shape it can close in.

cells.tense: You're living in a version of this ending that hasn't happened yet, and you're drafting it line by line.
cells.verb: arranging how it has to go
cells.place: a clearing that keeps getting furnished before it's empty
cells.ask: Step back and say what kind of ending this is, in one sentence, with none of the details in it — and let the plan loosen until it's holding something again.
cells.core:
You're living in a version of this ending that hasn't happened yet, and you're drafting it line by line. The order of who hears what, the timeline, the conditions under which it's allowed to be over — the plan has gotten more real to you than the thing that's ending. The arranging was meant to make room. It's filling the room instead.

What helps isn't more arranging and it isn't dropping it; it's seeing the shape without the contents. Step back and say what kind of ending this is, in one sentence, with none of the details in it — and let the plan loosen until it's holding something again.
cells.sheetLine: The plan for the ending has gotten bigger than the ending.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already closed behind you.
cells.verb: never quite assembling the pieces of what's over into a finish
cells.place: a clearing where nothing got cleared
cells.ask: Pick one thing from what's over that was never going to hold and let it fall all at once, no sorting — and watch how the rest starts falling into order on its own.
cells.core:
You're still standing at a door that's already closed behind you. Something is over and it never became an ending — the pieces are all still here, unordered, and you can't tell which one goes first or what the finish would even look like. So nothing gets put away and nothing starts.

Trying harder to organize it won't do it; the organizing is the part that's empty. What has a current in it is the other move: collapse, not sorting. Pick one thing from what's over that was never going to hold and let it fall all at once, no sorting — and watch how the rest starts falling into order on its own.
cells.sheetLine: It's over. It never got to be an ending.

cells.tense: You're already in this room, pen in hand, and you've put the pen down to say you've got no part in it.
cells.verb: holding the shape of how it ends
cells.place: a clearing other people are walking through on your lines
cells.ask: Name one ending you've been holding the shape of as yours to hold — and let it actually finish, with you as the one who finished it.
cells.core:
You're already in this room, pen in hand, and you've put the pen down to say you've got no part in it. People around you are getting through this ending because of an order you provided — what to let go of, in what sequence, where to stop — and you'd describe yourself as the one who has no idea what's happening. The structure is yours. The feeling of having none is the only part that's off.

The way back is smaller than it sounds: let one thing finish on purpose. Name one ending you've been holding the shape of as yours to hold — and let it actually finish, with you as the one who finished it.
cells.sheetLine: They're getting through this on your order. You call it having none.
